god.limits: Screening level at 5 km. Uses map-scale aquifer types and BGS depth classes, not local borehole logs; confining layers, soils and land use are not mapped. Not for site decisions.

recharge.ref: MacDonald et al. (2021) Mapping groundwater recharge in Africa from ground observations and implications for water security. Environ. Res. Lett. 16 034012; dataset doi 10.5285/45d2b71c-d413-44d4-8b4b-6190527912ff
recharge.limits: Long-term average (1970-2019) at about 30 km; local recharge varies with soils, land cover and rainfall intensity.

stress.ref: Groundwater Development Stress (GDS) = abstraction / recharge x 100% (IGRAC, UN World Water Development Report 2015).
stress.limits: The atlas estimates domestic abstraction only: population x share using boreholes (DHS) x litres per person per day chosen by the user. Irrigation, industry and wells are not included, so true stress is higher.

baseflow.ref: Lyne & Hollick (1979) digital filter, alpha 0.925, three passes with reflected padding (Ladson et al. 2013, Australian Journal of Water Resources 17:25-34).
baseflow.limits: Applied to modelled GloFAS v4 daily discharge, whose groundwater stores come from the LISFLOOD model, not observed gauge records. On large rivers the slow component also includes floodplain, wetland and reservoir storage, not only groundwater. Use as an indicator of slow, sustained flow, not a measured groundwater contribution. The correlation is Spearman's rank correlation between mean baseflow in April (end of the dry season) and that year's peak flow.
